name: San Antonio
metroName: San Antonio-New Braunfels, TX Metropolitan Statistical Area (CBSA 41700; OMB July 2023 delineation: Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, Comal, Guadalupe, Kendall, Medina and Wilson counties)

electric.name: CPS Energy
electric.serves: City of San Antonio-owned utility (since 1942), which CPS describes as 'the nation's largest municipally owned energy utility providing both natural gas and electric service.' It serves 'more than 996,000 electric and 399,000 natural gas customers in San Antonio and portions of seven adjoining counties' (main body of its About page; the page's meta description gives older figures). CPS sells and delivers power itself and runs its own efficiency plan (STEP).

gas.name: CPS Energy (natural gas)
gas.serves: Same city-owned utility provides natural gas in San Antonio and parts of adjoining counties.

utilities.notes: CPS Energy is municipally owned and sells and delivers electricity to its own customers. Under PUCT rules, municipal utilities decide for themselves whether to join Texas retail competition, so the PUCT Power to Choose marketplace and the wires-company efficiency model used in Dallas and Houston do not describe CPS territory. CPS has its own efficiency program, the Sustainable Tomorrow Energy Plan (STEP): a $350 million, 5-year plan authorized by San Antonio City Council Ordinance 2022-06-16-0435 on June 16, 2022. Rebates are paid by CPS (usually as a bill credit or check to the account holder) rather than routed through a wires company. The current rebate forms cover 'program dates: February 1, 2026–January 31, 2027' (labeled PY5). CPS's fiscal year runs Feb 1 to Jan 31. All current STEP residential rebates are for electric measures; no CPS natural-gas appliance rebates were found on its rebate pages. Outlying parts of the 8-county MSA are served by other municipal utilities or electric cooperatives, which were not researched here.

auditPrograms.name: CPS Energy No-Cost Home Energy Assessment (in-home)
auditPrograms.runBy: CPS Energy (STEP), delivered by a CPS Energy Home Energy Advisor through program implementer CLEAResult
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Current CPS Energy residential customers (account holders). An adult 18+ must be present. 'Apartment complexes do not qualify.'
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A 1–2 hour visit identifying energy waste and comfort fixes. Free energy-saving products such as LED bulbs and smart power strips (up to a $125 value). A personalized report with recommendations. Rebates for qualifying improvements through a participating contractor, 'up to $435 for homes with central AC and non-electric heating.' CPS's FY2026 Q4 STEP report says the visit may include installing advanced power strips, faucet aerators, low-flow showerheads, LED lighting and smart thermostats.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online at cpsenergy.clearesult.com (verify eligibility, request an appointment, schedule, then 'place order' at $0), or call 210-353-2728.
auditPrograms.status: Open. Listed 'In stock' at $0 with an active booking flow on 2026-10-12.

auditPrograms.name: CPS Energy Virtual Home Energy Assessment
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Current CPS Energy residential customers; an adult 18+ must video chat with the advisor. Apartment complexes do not qualify.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: Smartphone video walk-through with a CPS Energy advisor after a 15–30 minute pre-assessment call. Free energy-saving products (LEDs, smart power strips, up to $125) are mailed afterward. Personalized report; the same contractor rebate eligibility as the in-home version.
auditPrograms.status: Open (booking flow live 2026-10-12; the page shows both 'In stock' and 'Out Of Stock' labels, so confirm at checkout).

auditPrograms.name: Casa Verde Weatherization (assessment by a registered Trade Ally)
auditPrograms.cost: No participant cost stated. CPS Energy 'will rebate the cost of all eligible upgrades.'
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Income-qualifying homeowners and renters. 2026 gross monthly income limits: 1 person < $2,660; 2 < $3,607; 3 < $4,554; 4 < $5,550; 5 < $6,447; 6 < $7,394; 7 < $8,340; 8 < $9,287; +$947 each additional person. Also qualifies: energy burden of 10%+ of annual income, or receipt of income-based assistance.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A home assessment by a registered Trade Ally, then upgrades: attic, wall and floor insulation; air infiltration reduction; duct sealing/repair; WiFi smart thermostats; central A/C tune-ups; LED bulbs; low-flow showerheads and aerators; solar screens; window A/C replacement.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online application ('Begin application') or paper form; choose a registered Trade Ally. Help line 210-353-CASA (2272).
auditPrograms.status: Unverified. The application link is live, but the page states no open/closed or waitlist status.

auditPrograms.name: AACOG Weatherization Assistance Program (Bexar and 10 other Alamo-region counties)
auditPrograms.runBy: Alamo Area Council of Governments (TDHCA's WAP subrecipient for Bexar County)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Income-eligible households under federal guidelines (no dollar figure on the page); U.S. citizens or eligible resident aliens. The home must be structurally sound (no roof damage or faulty wiring); WAP 'does not cover major home repairs.'
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: Draft sealing, insulation, duct sealing or heating/cooling replacement, and indoor air quality assessment.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Complete the 2026 WAP application PDF, call (210) 362-5282, or email wap@aacog.gov.
auditPrograms.status: Unverified. The page states no waitlist or closure. A 2026 application form is posted, and AACOG lists a Weatherization Program Lunch & Learn on Oct 30, 2026.

rebates.name: CPS Energy HVAC Rebates: central A/C, heat pumps, mini-splits (STEP)
rebates.amount: Per cooling ton. Early Replacement (working system under 25 yrs for central A/C, under 20 yrs for heat pumps): 13.8–15.1 SEER2 $115; 15.2–16.1 $130; 16.2–17.0 $175; 17.1–19.9 $250; 20.0+ $310. Replace on Burnout: $90; $120; $150; $225; $275 for the same tiers. Rebate cannot exceed project cost.
rebates.whoQualifies: Residential CPS Energy account holders (single-family up to fourplex; tenants need owner permission). Not available for new homes. One-for-one retrofit installed by a Texas-licensed HVAC contractor. Minimums: A/C 14.3 SEER2/11.7 EER2 (<45,000 BTUh); heat pumps 14.3 SEER2/11.7 EER2/7.5 HSPF2. A permit number is required inside San Antonio city limits.
rebates.status: Open for program dates Feb 1, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027 (PY5), first-come, first-served, 'subject to change or cancellation without notice'. Apply within 30 days of installation. Paid as a bill credit (2–3 weeks) or check (8–12 weeks).

rebates.name: CPS Energy Window A/C Rebate (STEP)
rebates.amount: $50 or $75 per ENERGY STAR room unit depending on size and CEER (e.g., louvered 20,000–27,999 BTU/hr at CEER 12.7: $75).
rebates.whoQualifies: CPS residential account holders; ENERGY STAR certified unit meeting CEER minimums.
rebates.status: Open, program dates Feb 1, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027; apply within 30 days.

rebates.name: CPS Energy Attic Insulation Rebate (STEP)
rebates.whoQualifies: CPS residential account holders. Insulation must sit between air-conditioned living space and an unconditioned attic. With more than 24 in. attic clearance: final level at least R-38, existing no greater than R-14. With less clearance: final R-19+, existing no greater than R-11. Garages and other non-living areas don't qualify. Dated itemized receipt required.
rebates.status: Open, program dates Feb 1, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027; file within 30 days of completion.

rebates.name: CPS Energy Cool Roof Rebate (STEP)
rebates.amount: Per sq ft: low slope, solar reflectance 0.50–<0.70 $0.08, 0.70+ $0.20. High slope, 0.15–<0.50 $0.08, 0.50+ $0.20.
rebates.whoQualifies: CRRC-listed products; at least 75% of the roof surface replaced; home must have functioning electric A/C and no significant shading.
rebates.status: Open, program dates Feb 1, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027; file within 30 days.

rebates.name: CPS Energy Variable-Speed Pool Pump Rebate (STEP)
rebates.amount: '$50/hp, up to $150' (rounded to nearest half hp; not to exceed project cost).
rebates.whoQualifies: New ENERGY STAR variable-speed pump with 1-year+ warranty, one-for-one replacement. New pools, motor-only swaps and rebuilds excluded.

rebates.name: CPS Energy WiFi Thermostat Rewards (demand response)
rebates.amount: '$85 one-time rebate for each thermostat you enroll' plus 'a $30 bill credit per business or household account' after each summer season while enrolled.
rebates.whoQualifies: Customers who install and enroll a CPS-approved WiFi thermostat (Google Nest except Gen 1–2, Honeywell Home, ecobee, Sensi, Amazon, etc.) and allow brief adjustments during peak demand. CPS-installed thermostats don't qualify.
rebates.status: Open for enrollment ('subject to change without prior notice').

rebates.name: CPS Energy High-Performance A/C Tune-up
rebates.amount: 'no-cost High-Performance A/C Tune-up' for qualifiers. The customer pays for a filter if needed, and any recommended repairs are extra and optional.
rebates.whoQualifies: Residential customers in single-family homes in CPS territory with a working central A/C or heat pump at least one year old. No program tune-up in the past five years. Mini-splits and window units are excluded.
rebates.status: Registration form live; open/closed status not stated (requires an outdoor temperature of at least 55°F).

rebates.name: City of San Antonio Under 1 Roof: Cool Roofs for High-Heat Areas
rebates.runBy: City of San Antonio Neighborhood and Housing Services Department
rebates.amount: '0% interest, forgivable loans' up to $19,000 for energy-efficient cool-roof shingle replacement, with a 5-year restrictive covenant. The loan is forgiven over time while the owner stays; the balance plus interest is due if the owner moves, rents or sells early.
rebates.whoQualifies: Owner-occupants of single-family homes in a Cool Roofs covered area (Urban Heat Island priority map). Household income at or below 80% AMI (limits updated June 1, 2026). Also requires a homestead exemption, current taxes and mortgage, clear title (liens under $5,000 allowed) and homeowner's insurance. No reverse mortgages.
rebates.status: Restricted. NHSD 'is only accepting Cool Roof appointments from San Antonio homeowners living in an Urban Heat Island Neighborhood'. Processing can take up to 3 months. Not for emergency roof replacement.

stateHomeEnergyRebates.status: Not launched. SECO says 'Rebates are not currently available.' The programs are being designed in fall 2026, and 'A launch date has not been set and will depend on DOE approval of the final program design.'
stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Texas HOMES and HEAR Rebate programs (Home Efficiency Rebates, HOMES; Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates, HEAR)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, State Energy Conservation Office (SECO). Implementer: APTIM Federal Services, LLC, hired April 2026.
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: $690 million DOE allocation. HOMES will be open to all incomes; HEAR is limited to households below 150% of AMI. Amounts are not yet set, and HOMES levels are under DOE review. Projects completed before launch are unlikely to qualify. The FAQ says the implementer will work with local partners statewide; no municipal-utility carve-out was described.

incomeQualified.name: Weatherization Assistance Program, Bexar County and Alamo region
incomeQualified.summary: Free WAP for income-eligible residents of Bexar, Atascosa, Bandera, Comal, Guadalupe, Kendall, Medina, Wilson and other Alamo-region counties: sealing, insulation, duct/HVAC work, indoor air quality assessment. (210) 362-5282, wap@aacog.gov. AACOG also runs the Amy Young Barrier Removal grant, Warm Hearts Warm Homes space heaters for people 60+, and Homes for Texas Heroes repairs and weatherization for low-income veterans.

incomeQualified.name: CPS Energy Casa Verde Weatherization
incomeQualified.summary: Rebate-funded whole-home weatherization (insulation, air and duct sealing, smart thermostat, A/C tune-up, solar screens and more) for income-qualified homeowners and renters. 2026 limit for one person is under $2,660/month gross. STEP's goal is to weatherize 16,000 homes over 5 years. Phone 210-353-2272.

incomeQualified.name: City of San Antonio Under 1 Roof (cool roofs)
incomeQualified.summary: Forgivable 0% loan up to $19,000 for a cool-roof replacement for owner-occupants at or below 80% AMI in Urban Heat Island neighborhoods. NHSD's repair menu also lists Green & Healthy Homes (lead, asthma and fire hazards in pre-1978 homes with young children, at or below 80% AMI), a Minor Repair Loan and a Major Rehab Forgivable Loan.

incomeQualified.name: Bill assistance (CEAP) and community services in Bexar County
incomeQualified.runBy: Bexar County Department of Community Resources (CEAP); City of San Antonio Department of Human Services (CSBG), per TDHCA
incomeQualified.summary: TDHCA's 2/2/2026 subrecipient list routes Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (utility bill help) for Bexar County to the county's Department of Community Resources. WAP goes to AACOG.

localRules.name: No energy audit, disclosure-at-sale or private-building benchmarking requirement in San Antonio
localRules.summary: No City of San Antonio requirement for home energy audits, disclosure at sale or private-building benchmarking was found. ACEEE's State & Local Policy Database (non-government; sections last updated Sept 2023) says the city benchmarks its own buildings 'Although a benchmarking policy is not in place,' and reports San Antonio adopted the 2021 IECC effective February 2023 (a new-construction code, not a requirement on existing homes).

notes: San Antonio is the strongest of the Texas metros here for market-rate homeowners. CPS Energy pays rebates directly to its customers (bill credit or check) and offers a free in-home or virtual energy assessment open to all residential customers, not only low-income ones. Surprising: CPS Energy 'does not currently offer rebates for residential solar installations'. Its residential solar page still points homeowners to the federal Residential Clean Energy Credit, which the IRS says is not allowed for expenditures after Dec 31, 2025, so that CPS page is out of date. CPS 'Hosted solar' is 'Fully Subscribed'; Community Solar is 'Now Accepting Enrollments'. STEP is a 5-year, $350M plan authorized June 16, 2022. Its current program dates run to Jan 31, 2027, and no successor plan was found on CPS's site. The federal 25C credit (including the $150 audit allowance) ended for property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025, and Texas HOMES/HEAR rebates have not launched. Unverified: Casa Verde's current intake status; AACOG WAP waitlist; what follows STEP after its 5-year term.
